title: The Ethics of Influence - Chapter 3 As Judged by Themselves
excerpt: Chapter 3 develops the welfare criterion behind [[Ethics of Nudging]]: a nudge should generally make choosers better off as judged by themselves. This is not the same as satisfying whatever people happen to choose in a poorly informed, impulsive, or manipulate

title: The Ethics of Influence - Chapter 4 Values
excerpt: Chapter 4 is the book's compact ethical framework for nudging. Sunstein evaluates nudges through four values: welfare, autonomy, dignity, and self-government. The point is not that nudges automatically satisfy these values because they preserve formal choice.

title: The Ethics of Influence - Chapter 5 Fifty Shades of Manipulation
